t: Check if There Is a Valid Parentheses String Path — DP on Balance
o: Any down/right path from (0,0) to (m-1,n-1) has exactly m+n-1 cells. A parentheses string built from such a path is valid iff every prefix has balance (#open minus #close) >= 0 and the final balance is 0. So we do grid DP where the state includes the running balance: reachable[i][j][b] = true if some path to (i,j) has balance b. Balance never exceeds m+n and never goes negative, giving O(m*n*(m+n)) states — about 2 million for 100x100, easily fast enough.
k: Path validity reduces to tracking the prefix balance; negative balance kills a path immediately.
DP dimensions: cell (i, j) x balance b, with transitions from top and left neighbors.

a.i: Process cells in row-major order. From each reachable (cell, balance) state, moving onto '(' raises the balance by 1, ')' lowers it by 1 (discarding negative balances). Answer is whether (m-1, n-1) is reachable with balance 0.
s: Create dp[i][j] as a bitset/array over balances 0..m+n.
Seed dp[0][0] with balance 1 if grid[0][0]=='(' else unreachable (balance -1 invalid).
Transition: dp[i][j][b + delta] |= dp[i-1][j][b] | dp[i][j-1][b], delta = +1 for '(', -1 for ')', only if b+delta >= 0.
a.t: O(m*n*(m+n)) — every cell iterates over all possible balances.
a.sp: O(m*n*(m+n)) for the DP table; reducible to O(n*(m+n)) with rolling rows.

a.i: Represent the set of reachable balances per cell as a big integer bitmask: bit b set means balance b is achievable. Shifting the mask left/right implements the +/-1 transition in one operation, cutting constant factors dramatically in Python and C++.
s: dp[i][j] is an integer bitmask over balances.
Transition: mask = ((fromTop | fromLeft) shifted by delta) masked to valid range.
Check bit 0 of the final cell.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def hasValidPath(self, grid: List[List[str]]) -> bool:
        m, n = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        if grid[0][0] != '(' or grid[m-1][n-1] != ')':
            return False
        full = (1 << (m + n + 1)) - 1
        dp = [[0] * n for _ in range(m)]
        dp[0][0] = 1 << 1
        for i in range(m):
            for j in range(n):
                d = 1 if grid[i][j] == '(' else -1
                cur = 0
                if i > 0: cur |= dp[i-1][j]
                if j > 0: cur |= dp[i][j-1]
                if i == 0 and j == 0: cur = dp[0][0]
                shifted = (cur << 1) | (cur >> 1) if False else ((cur << 1) if d == 1 else (cur >> 1))
                dp[i][j] = shifted & full if i or j else dp[0][0]
        return (dp[m-1][n-1] & 1) != 0

a.t: O(m*n*(m+n)/64) word operations — bit tricks parallelize the balance dimension.

w: Always check the corner cells first: if either is wrong the answer is immediately false. The main pitfall is letting the balance go negative or forgetting the final balance must be exactly 0. Follow-up: count the number of valid paths (same DP with counts instead of booleans, modulo a prime).
